_note: The pallet-built studio from the reference photo, set up for mixing from this room's own acoustics (npm run mix): a poured concrete building with plastered concrete walls, modern double glazing and a tiled floor, all of which absorb little bass, so the bare room rings for about 3.4 s at 63-125 Hz and the windows are where most of the bass escapes. Facing the solid back wall, so every early reflection from the front lands on plaster that can be treated, and the street glass is behind the listener. Listening position on the centreline 4.16 m (36%) from the back wall with a 1.35 m equilateral triangle, the flattest bass in the 30-45% band however much furnishing the room holds; Rokit 7 G4 monitors on stands, toed in 30 deg. Treatment: reflection panels on the back wall and the mural wall at the first-reflection points, free-standing panels in front of the window where the other side reflection falls on glass, corner bass traps in the back corners, four membrane traps tuned to the 45 Hz length mode (two on the back wall, two on the mural wall where that mode peaks), the ceiling covered with fitted panels (coverCeiling), rugs on the tiles under the mix position and the lounge, and heavy curtains on the two street windows behind the listener, drawn when mixing to take that glass reflection; open, they stack on the piers and leave the glass clear. With every hard surface in the room, the whole ceiling and both rugs are what bring the mids to EBU Tech 3276's 0.28 s; half the ceiling leaves about 0.5 s. The lounge sits at the street end. Metres from the room centre; ry in degrees.
name: Pallet studio
